image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) floating on greenish water. The duck features a characteristic iridescent green head, a white neck ring, a yellow bill, and a brown chest with grey and brown patterned body plumage. One orange webbed foot is visible paddling in the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and yellow-green in color, matching the description perfectly.
The eye is visible against the dark green head feathers and appears dark/black.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is consistent with a floating duck, appearing streamlined and buoyant. Plumage texture looks dense and waterproof.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and brown/grey body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One orange leg/foot is visible in the water. It shows clear webbing between toes, consistent with aquatic bird anatomy.
The folded wings on the side of the body appear broad and taper towards the tail, consistent with the 'broad and pointed' description when at rest.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is short, and the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (sexually dimorphic trait of mallard drakes) is clearly visible.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Mallard Drake) and rule out hybrid or nonsensical bird features.
To verify the structural integrity of the visible leg and foot, ensuring no fusion or extra digits despite partial occlusion by water.
To check for edge bleeding or melting where the duck's body meets the water surface, a common AI artifact in floating subjects.
To assess the realism of feather details and ensure no smearing or unnatural patterns in the iridescent head feathers.

focus_areas: Webbing structure of the visible foot
Boundary sharpness between duck body and water
Iridescent texture consistency on the head
Anatomical correctness of the curled tail feathers
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the visible foot in the water. AI often struggles with webbed feet, either merging toes or creating too many. Verify if the visible webbing looks physically plausible. Also, inspect the white neck ring for any bleeding into the green head or brown chest, which would indicate segmentation errors.
